snippet.title: What Really Happens to Your Stuff After an EMP & (the 7 Things That Still Work)
snippet.description:
📩 FREE DOWNLOAD → The 50 Dollar Food Plan (build 90 days of shelf-stable food for your family for about $50): https://zachofalltrades.io/freeplan/


There is probably no topic in preparedness culture that has been distorted by fiction more than the electromagnetic pulse.

The EMP, in the popular imagination, is the ultimate reset button. Every electronic device in the country dies instantly. Every car stops on the highway. Every phone goes dark. The grid comes down and stays down for years. Civilization reverts overnight to a 19th-century state.

That version comes from novels, movies, and prep content that has borrowed from novels and movies. It is not what the actual physics or the actual engineering research suggests would happen.

The real picture is more nuanced, less dramatic in some ways, more serious in others, and worth understanding accurately if you want to prepare intelligently. Not because I want to convince you EMPs are not worth worrying about — the risk is real, and the topic deserves a place in any complete preparedness plan. But because the fictional version has led millions of families to prepare for the wrong scenario in the wrong way, and clearer thinking about what would actually happen produces better preparedness.

This video walks through what would actually happen after a real EMP event — the different types of EMP, the real effects on the electrical grid, and where the fictional version departs from what the engineering and government research suggests. Then it walks through 7 specific categories of things that would still work in the aftermath.

What we cover:

— The 3 components of a nuclear EMP (E1, E2, E3) and why each does something different
— The 1859 Carrington Event and what it did to the telegraph network (with details most people never learn)
— The 1989 Quebec blackout — 6 million people, 9 hours, from a much smaller solar event than Carrington
— Why the real infrastructure vulnerability is large power transformers (not your phone in your pocket)
— Category 1: The Air Force EMP vehicle testing results (spoiler: most cars would still run)
— Category 2: Why disconnected electronics survive at dramatically higher rates (and the $50 Faraday cage anyone can build this weekend)
— Category 3: The tool category that is completely immune to any EMP
— Category 4: The heating and cooking capability that would matter enormously
— Category 5: The food preparation methods your great-grandparents used that would still work
— Category 6: The category almost every family forgets entirely
— Category 7: The single most important category on the entire list (and no gear can replace it)
— 3 things to do this week — under $50 — that address the actual shape of EMP preparedness

This is calm, grounded, research-informed preparedness for a topic that has been dramatized so heavily in popular culture that clear thinking about it has become genuinely rare. No doom. No hype. No fictional grid-down-forever framing. Just the honest engineering picture of what would actually happen — and the specific practical steps that produce real resilience against this scenario and every other extended grid disruption.

snippet.title: @adamwolfefitness if you’re looking for a simple one pan meal prep this is a great option #mealprep
snippet.description:
2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bitesized pieces
1½ cups jasmine rice, uncooked
1 can (10 oz) mild red enchilada sauce
1 3/4 cups chicken broth
1 medium yellow onion, diced
1 red bell pepper, diced
1 cup corn, drained
2 CUPS
1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 small can mild diced green chiles
2 tbsp minced garlic
100g reduced-fat Mexican-blend cheese
Seasoning blend:
2 tsp chili powder
1½ tsp ground cumin
1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp dried oregano

Directions:
1. ﻿﻿﻿Preheat your oven to 400°F.
2. ﻿﻿﻿Grab a 9x13 baking dish - add the chicken breasts, 1½ cups uncooked jasmine rice, diced onion, bell pepper, corn, black beans, green chiles and minced garlic directly to the baking dish.
3. ﻿﻿﻿Season with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, oregano, salt and black pepper.
Pour in the 10-ounce can of enchilada sauce, 1 3/4 cups of warm chicken broth
1. ﻿﻿﻿Spread it into an even layer and make sure the rice is submerged beneath the liquid.
2. ﻿﻿﻿Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake at
400°F for 45 minutes.

1. ﻿﻿﻿Remove the foil and sprinkle 150g of reduced-fat Mexican-blend cheese evenly over the top.
2. ﻿﻿﻿Return it to the oven uncovered for another
10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, the rice is tender and the chicken has reached
165°F.
1. ﻿﻿﻿Let it rest for 10 minutes so the rice can absorb the remaining liquid.
2. ﻿﻿﻿Divide into six servings and finish with your favorite toppings. Serve hot & enjoy!

snippet.title: Why is the UK telling people to stockpile? | BBC News
snippet.description:
Major retailers have reported a big rise in sales of tinned food, bottled water, wind up radios and batteries, after the government launched its 'be ready' campaign.

The government is urging people to stock up on enough for three days in case of a crisis - like extreme weather or a cyber-attack. 

The security minister's defended the campaign, arguing that our European neighbours seem better prepared.
